findings.description: The runtime-drift loop now depends on `$TARGET_ROOT/$rel_dir/install-manifest.json` existing in every mirror. When it does not (a mirror synced by a pre-manifest install.sh, a mirror whose manifest was deleted, or, per open ledger 40, an agent in the CLI `agent_list` that was never installed), payload_hash.py exits 2 and the only output is the generic 'Cannot compute mirror payload hash for <agent>'. That is a legitimate drift condition (mirror no longer matches the pinned payload) but it is neither the spec's runtime-drift message naming the pinned `toolkit_version`/`source_commit` nor a hint about the missing manifest. Before invoking the helper, test for the mirror manifest: if absent, print the runtime-drift message with a 'mirror manifest missing' qualifier (and skip the agent entirely when it is not listed in the stamp's `agents`, which also closes ledger 40).
findings.resolution: Guard with `[[ -f "$TARGET_ROOT/$rel_dir/install-manifest.json" ]]` and emit the runtime-drift message (pinned version/commit) instead of the generic hash error; drive the agent loop from the stamp's `agents` field.

    assert result.returncode == 1
    assert "Checkout drift" in result.stderr
    assert "Runtime drift" not in result.stderr
findings.description: The new test correctly fails against the pre-fix code (checkout B's manifest drops json-canvas, so the mirror hash no longer equals the stamp and 'Runtime drift' is printed). But its negative assertions are loose: if install.sh stopped syncing `install-manifest.json` into the mirrors, payload_hash.py would exit 2, stderr would read 'Cannot compute mirror payload hash', the exit code would still be 1 and 'Checkout drift' would still be present, so the test would pass while the feature it pins is broken. Add `assert "Cannot compute" not in result.stderr` (or assert the exact expected stderr lines) so the test only passes on the intended path. Also note the hard-coded dependency on `json-canvas` being portable in the real manifest; the explicit `assert manifest["skills"]["json-canvas"] == ...` makes that coupling fail loudly, which is acceptable, but picking the first portable skill from the manifest would make the test independent of that skill's future scoping.

findings.description: Fourteen pre-existing ledger entries change only in the relative order of `resolution`, `parked_reason` and `consensus_status`, with identical values. The ledger writer serialises keys in insertion order rather than a stable order, so every round that touches an entry re-emits unrelated entries and inflates the diff reviewers must read. The substantive additions (35 and 48 addressed with the 000c2bc reference, 36 retired as an echo of 10, 37-47 and 49 opened) are correct and consistent with the spec; the open items listed for re-verification are untouched by this diff and remain open. Consider `json.dump(..., sort_keys=True)` or a fixed key order in the ledger writer so future rounds diff only what changed.
